edge.label: Attacker leverages default system credentials or discovered credentials to obtain authenticated low-privilege web session on piSignage

source_node.label: Raspberry Pi OS Default Credentials Exploitation
source_node.precondition: Target Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS version <= 5.10 accessible over network or local console with default 'pi' account and 'raspberry' password unchanged.
source_node.postcondition: Attacker obtains authenticated administrative (sudo/root) access to the Raspberry Pi OS environment.

target_node.label: piSignage Arbitrary File Download (Path Traversal)
target_node.precondition: piSignage version < 2.6.4 running on target Raspberry Pi; attacker possesses authenticated low-privilege user credentials for the web application.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker reads and downloads arbitrary files from the host Raspberry Pi filesystem via api/settings/log?file=../, potentially exposing sensitive configuration files and credentials.

source.description: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 has the raspberry default password for the pi account. If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges.

applicability_rule.note: The record does not name a remote service (e.g. SSH); network reachability of the host is assumed.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.

applicability_rule.note: Arbitrary file read only; the record does not say what the files contain, so no foothold is granted.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

edge.label: Attacker uses default/administrative credentials to authenticate to RaspAP interface hosting webconsole.php

source_node.label: Raspberry Pi OS Default Credentials Exploitation

target_node.label: RaspAP Web Console Command Execution
target_node.precondition: RaspAP version 2.5 installed; attacker has authenticated access to the web interface with access to includes/webconsole.php.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker executes arbitrary OS-level commands, uploads files, and runs malicious code on the underlying Raspberry Pi operating system.

source.description: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 has the raspberry default password for the pi account. If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges.

applicability_rule.note: The record does not name a remote service (e.g. SSH); network reachability of the host is assumed.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target.description: An issue was discovered in includes/webconsole.php in RaspAP 2.5. With authenticated access, an attacker can use a misconfigured (and virtually unrestricted) web console to attack the underlying OS (Raspberry Pi) running this software, and execute commands on the system (including ones for uploading of files and execution of code).

applicability_rule.note: Privilege of the executed commands is not stated in the record, so only a user-level foothold is granted.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

edge.label: Attacker transitions from remote code execution in Oculus Browser to local unprivileged execution, setting up hard links for OVRRedir.exe abuse

source_node.label: Oculus Browser HTML UI Injection and Code Execution
source_node.precondition: Oculus Browser versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11 running; user visits an attacker-controlled remote web page.
source_node.postcondition: Attacker injects arbitrary HTML into the Oculus Browser UI, achieving UI spoofing and executing code within the unprivileged user context on the host system.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hard Link Arbitrary File Write
target_node.precondition: Oculus Desktop version < 1.44.0.32849 installed on Windows; attacker has unprivileged local code execution/file system access.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker creates a hard link to target critical system files from an unprivileged log file written by privileged OVRRedir.exe, enabling arbitrary file overwrite and local privilege escalation to SYSTEM.

source.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

applicability_rule.note: 'potentially execute code': user-level foothold is the generous reading. Requires the victim to open an attacker-controlled page (inferred from 'remote web page').
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target.description: Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

applicability_rule.note: The CVE record's version field has a typo (1.44.0.328549); the description is used. 'gain privileges' is read as admin.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher Process Handle Leak
target_node.precondition: Oculus Desktop versions between 1.39 and 31.1.0.67.507 installed on Windows; attacker has unprivileged local process execution rights.
target_node.postcondition: Privileged process handle exposed to an unprivileged process via handle management bug, allowing attacker to manipulate privileged processes and achieve local privilege escalation.

source.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

applicability_rule.note: 'potentially execute code': user-level foothold is the generous reading. Requires the victim to open an attacker-controlled page (inferred from 'remote web page').

target.description: Due to a bug with management of handles in OVRServiceLauncher.exe, an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.

applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions
